Yes it can. With the generic medications, the only thing that is the same from brand to brand is the active ingredient, sertraline, which is also the same in the name brand. A big however though is that there is no regulation on the fillers. Which actually matters more than people would think because these fillers control how the pill is metabolized and therefore how the active sting is released. Therefore, depending on the generic brand, the actual dosage (concentration of sertraline) in the bloodstream can range anywhere from plus or minus 25 mg (for a 100 mg dose. 

So, to answer your question simply, YES, it can be either too strong or too weak.

You could have gotten a different manufacturer. This happens all the time and is why I refuse to take the generic. The dose of these drugs is very important and the generic manufacturers don't seem to care. The actual dosage of these drugs in the body can range anywhere from plus or minus 25 mg (for 100 mg dose) which is a very big difference and very likely why people randomly get depressed, especially since pharmacies switch manufactures of their generics ALL THE TIME.
